final_answer: The 2008 financial crisis began with subprime mortgages, which were high-risk loans given to borrowers with poor credit histories. These mortgages were bundled into mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and collateralized debt obligations (CDOs), which were sold to investors worldwide. Rating agencies mistakenly labeled many of these as low-risk, despite their inherent instability. When housing prices peaked and began to fall, borrowers defaulted on their loans, causing the value of MBS and CDOs to collapse. Banks and financial institutions that held these securities faced massive losses, triggering a liquidity crisis. The collapse of Lehman Brothers in September 2008 marked a turning point, leading to a loss of confidence in financial markets. This cascading failure resulted in a credit freeze, bank failures, and a global recession. Governments intervened with bailouts and stimulus measures to stabilize the system.
